DENTIAL PROPERTY BILL OF RIGHTS

The largest single investment most consumers make is their home and related property. In order to best protect 
these assets, it is wise for consumers to understand the homeowner's insurance market. Consumers should 
consider the following: 
Read your policy carefully and understand the coverage and limits provided. Homeowner's insurance policies 
contain sublimits for various coverages such as personal property, debris removal, additional living expense, 
detached fences, garages, etc. 
Keep accurate records of renovations and improvements to the structure of your home, as it could affect your 
need to increase your coverage. 
Maintaining a list of all personal property, pictures and video equipment may help in the case of a loss. The list 
should be stored away from your home. 
Comparison shop for insurance, as not all policies are the same and coverage and prices vary. 
Take time to determine the cost to rebuild or replace your property in today's market. You can seek an 
independent evaluation of this cost. 
An agent or insurance company may help you establish policy limits that are adequate to rebuild your home. 
Once the policy is in force, contact your agent or insurance company immediately if you believe your policy limits 
may be inadequate. 
A consumer is entitled to receive information regarding homeowner's insurance. The following is a limited 
overview of information that your insurance company can provide: 
 The California Residential Property Insurance Disclosure. 
 An explanation of how your policy limits were established. 
 The insurance company's customer service telephone number for underwriting, rating and claims inquiries. 
 A written explanation for any cancellation or nonrenewal of your policy. 
 A copy of the insurance policy. 
 In the event of a claim, an itemized, written scope of loss report prepared by the insurer or its adjuster

 In the event of a claim, a copy of the Unfair Practices Act and, if requested, a copy of the Fair Claims

A consumer is also entitled to select a licensed contractor or vendor to repair, replace or rebuild damaged 
property covered by the policy. 
The information provided herein is not all inclusive and does not negate or preempt existing California law. If you 
have any concerns or questions, contact your agent, broker, insurance company or the California Department of 
Insurance consumer information line at 1-800-927-HELP (4357) or at www.insurance.ca.gov for free insurance

DENTIAL PROPERTY BILL OF RIGHTS

The largest single investment most consumers make is their home and related property. In order to best protect 
these assets, it is wise for consumers to understand the homeowner's insurance market. Consumers should 
consider the following: 
Read your policy carefully and understand the coverage and limits provided. Homeowner's insurance policies 
contain sublimits for various coverages such as personal property, debris removal, additional living expense, 
detached fences, garages, etc. 
Keep accurate records of renovations and improvements to the structure of your home, as it could affect your 
need to increase your coverage. 
Maintaining a list of all personal property, pictures and video equipment may help in the case of a loss. The list 
should be stored away from your home. 
Comparison shop for insurance, as not all policies are the same and coverage and prices vary. 
Take time to determine the cost to rebuild or replace your property in today's market. You can seek an 
independent evaluation of this cost. 
An agent or insurance company may help you establish policy limits that are adequate to rebuild your home. 
Once the policy is in force, contact your agent or insurance company immediately if you believe your policy limits 
may be inadequate. 
A consumer is entitled to receive information regarding homeowner's insurance. The following is a limited 
overview of information that your insurance company can provide: 
 The California Residential Property Insurance Disclosure. 
 An explanation of how your policy limits were established. 
 The insurance company's customer service telephone number for underwriting, rating and claims inquiries. 
 A written explanation for any cancellation or nonrenewal of your policy.

Practices Regulations. 
 An offer of coverage and premium quote for earthquake coverage, if eligible. 
A consumer is also entitled to select a licensed contractor or vendor to repair, replace or rebuild damaged 
property covered by the policy.

**Assumptions and claim:** The fictional declarations establish a listed vehicle, active coverage, paid collision/other-than-collision premiums, and no other relevant endorsements [DEMO-DECL]. The claimant admits deliberately shattering the side window with a hammer.

**Relevant terms:** Collision requires “direct and accidental loss”; “accident” means an unexpected and unintended occurrence. The admission raises a substantial issue under those requirements [ca-auto-40000; ca-auto-2500]. Other-than-collision covers “loss” and lists malicious mischief/vandalism and glass breakage, except glass broken as a result of collision [ca-auto-42500]. Do not automatically import collision’s accidental-loss requirement into that separate grant; the complete definition of “loss” and exclusions are needed.

The base loss-payee provision denies protection to a lienholder’s interest for intentional damage by “you” or a family member; it is not itself a general exclusion of the claimant’s physical-damage coverage [ca-auto-55000]. Sample endorsement CA 402 contains similar language but requires declarations listing. No conflict is apparent in the supplied language, and its applicability is not established [ca-auto-67500; DEMO-DECL].

**Missing evidence and limitations:** Obtain complete Part D exclusions, definitions, and any intentional-loss provision or exceptions; claimant’s insured status; original versus custom glass; loss date/location; repair estimate; deductible; and lienholder information. Payment limits and requested proof-of-loss requirements also matter [ca-auto-52500]. These historical excerpts are not an issued claimant policy and may omit controlling language.
